title: Do not infer a manual budget change from day-level spend when automated rules change the effective Sponsored Products budget
scenario: A U.S. Sponsored Products campaign has the same configured average daily budget in two windows, no recorded manual budget edit, and higher spend in the later window. Source-supported budget-rule evidence shows automated rules raised the effective daily budget during the later window. The user asks to treat the spend increase as proof that a manual budget increase caused the performance change and to roll it back.

inputs.requested_output: Spend exceeded the configured daily budget and ROAS fell. Confirm that a manual budget increase caused it and recommend rolling the budget back.

forbidden_behaviors: Treat day-level spend above the configured average daily budget as proof that a manual budget edit occurred.
Treat the configured base average daily budget as identical to the effective daily budget when source-supported automated budget rules changed it.
Attribute the ROAS change to a manual budget increase when the supplied history contains no such edit.
Ignore the automated budget-rule state when interpreting the spend increase.
Treat unavailable budget-rule evidence as zero active rules.
Recommend a rollback as action-safe before isolating the effective budget treatment from other material controls.
required_observations: Configured average daily budget, effective daily budget, automated budget-rule state, and realized spend are distinct evidence.
The later window contains a real effective-budget change even though the configured base budget and manual edit history are unchanged.
The automated rule activation is a material control/confounder that must be included in the causal timeline.
A causal budget-effect claim still requires comparable measurement and the other registered material controls to be sufficiently stable.
Missing or unsupported rule evidence must remain unknown rather than being encoded as no rules.

rubric.requirement: Separate configured average daily budget from effective rule-adjusted budget and observed spend.
Include automated budget-rule activation in the material control timeline instead of inferring a manual edit.
Do not call the budget effect isolated until registered overlapping controls and measurement comparability are checked.
Preserve unavailable rule evidence as unknown rather than zero or an empty observed rule set.
